answer: Random audit lottery draws 5 of every 100 onyx tickets each Monday, and a basalt audit log records each draw. Independent auditors check drawn agents against their claimed work, and a fake that fails pays $1,000 plus $1,000 for each sibling clone in the same river of payments, so one caught farm of 100 clones owes $100,000 while one honest agent owes $0 and keeps its $100 stake. A second fault in the quarter doubles the fine to $2,000 per clone, and a third burns the stake. Cloning stays a bad bet, the way a river wears soft stone down and leaves basalt standing.
